accepted.s: The primary objective of the BhashaNet portal is to promote which of the following?
accepted.x: BhashaNet was launched to promote digital inclusion by advancing Universal Acceptance, including support for diverse languages and scripts.
accepted.tq: Match the named initiative with its principal objective rather than a neighbouring ICT programme.
accepted.sec: Language and access - Bhashini, BhashaNet, Universal Acceptance, accessibility standards  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Universal Acceptance means that:
o: domain names and e-mail addresses in any language or script should function in every application
all internet services must be provided free of cost
all citizens must use one standard language on the internet
only government websites should accept Indian-language content
accepted.x: Universal Acceptance requires domain names and e-mail addresses in any language or script, including Indian-language domains, to work properly in every application.
accepted.tq: Test the precise definition of a confusable digital-access term.
accepted.sec: Language and access - Bhashini, BhashaNet, Universal Acceptance, accessibility standards  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Digital India Bhashini:
1. It is the National Language Translation Mission of MeitY.
2. It uses artificial intelligence for translation across Indian languages.
3. It is used in DARPG's SAMADHAN DIDI chatbot.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Bhashini is MeitY's National Language Translation Mission, uses AI-based translation, and supports the SAMADHAN DIDI chatbot of DARPG.
accepted.tq: Check several linked features of one mission before selecting the combined option.
accepted.sec: Language and access - Bhashini, BhashaNet, Universal Acceptance, accessibility standards  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Digital India Bhashini is associated with which of the following applications or systems?
1. DARPG's SAMADHAN DIDI chatbot
2. NIC's CollabFiles
3. The e-Gov App Store under MeghRaj
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Bhashini is used in the SAMADHAN DIDI chatbot and NIC's CollabFiles. The e-Gov App Store is part of MeghRaj architecture, not an application identified as using Bhashini.
accepted.tq: Separate applications of one technology from a related but different platform feature.
accepted.sec: Language and access - Bhashini, BhashaNet, Universal Acceptance, accessibility standards  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which guidelines prescribe accessibility norms for Indian Government websites?
accepted.x: GIGW, or Guidelines for Indian Government Websites, prescribe accessibility norms for government websites.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact official acronym from closely related digital-governance terms.
accepted.sec: Language and access - Bhashini, BhashaNet, Universal Acceptance, accessibility standards  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is the most appropriate e-governance response to accessibility barriers faced by elderly and disabled persons?
o: Requiring physical presence for every service
accepted.x: E-governance should provide assisted access so that elderly and disabled persons can use digital public services despite access barriers. Digital gender gaps and disability-related barriers continue to persist.
accepted.tq: Apply an inclusion principle to a practical service-delivery situation.
accepted.sec: Language and access - Bhashini, BhashaNet, Universal Acceptance, accessibility standards  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

List-I (Programme) — List-II (Description)
a. NDLM — i. Digital literacy scheme preceding PMGDISHA
b. DISHA — ii. Digital Saksharta Abhiyan
c. ICT@Schools — iii. Centrally sponsored scheme for computer labs and ICT learning

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: NDLM and DISHA refer to the digital literacy initiatives that preceded PMGDISHA, with DISHA expanded as Digital Saksharta Abhiyan. ICT@Schools was a centrally sponsored scheme for computer labs and ICT learning in government schools.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure acronym expansion and eliminate mismatched programme descriptions.
accepted.sec: Digital literacy missions - NDLM, DISHA, Vidya Vahini, ICT@Schools  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its focus?
o: e-Pathshala — optical-fibre connectivity to gram panchayats
Vidya Vahini — school project focused on computer education
accepted.x: Vidya Vahini was a school project focused on computer education. ICT@Schools concerned computer labs and ICT learning, NDLM concerned digital literacy, and e-Pathshala provided digital educational resources.
accepted.tq: Use nearby education and ICT schemes to detect the swapped programme descriptions.
accepted.sec: Digital literacy missions - NDLM, DISHA, Vidya Vahini, ICT@Schools  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about E&ICT Academy Phase-II:
1. It is associated with MeitY.
2. Its duration is five years.
3. It aims to train 1,35,000 faculty through 14 agencies.
4. The implementing agencies include IITs, NIT, NIELIT and CDAC.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. E&ICT Academy Phase-II is a five-year MeitY initiative targeting 1,35,000 faculty through 14 agencies, including IITs, NIT, NIELIT and CDAC.
accepted.tq: Verify the authority, duration, target and implementing-agency details together.
accepted.sec: Digital literacy missions - NDLM, DISHA, Vidya Vahini, ICT@Schools  [other exams]

accepted.s: e-Pathshala was launched in November 2015 by which combination of organisations?
accepted.x: e-Pathshala was launched in November 2015 by MHRD and NCERT to provide e-textbooks and other educational resources.
accepted.tq: Recall the implementing institutions and launch period of an education platform.
accepted.sec: Digital literacy missions - NDLM, DISHA, Vidya Vahini, ICT@Schools  [other exams]

accepted.s: The National Optical Fibre Network (NOFN), later associated with BharatNet, was approved on 25 October 2011 with an initial target of connecting:
accepted.x: NOFN was approved on 25 October 2011 with the objective of connecting 2.5 lakh gram panchayats.
accepted.tq: Recall the original programme name, date and numerical target together.
accepted.sec: BharatNet - phases, implementing agency, GP target, amended programme

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the institutional history of BharatNet's special purpose vehicle?
o: BBNL was registered on 25 February 2012 and merged with BSNL in February 2023.
BBNL was registered on 25 October 2011 and merged with RailTel in February 2023.
BBNL was registered in February 2023 and merged with BSNL in 2012.
BBNL was registered on 25 February 2012 and merged with PGCIL in February 2024.
accepted.x: Bharat Broadband Network Limited (BBNL) was registered on 25 February 2012 and merged with BSNL in February 2023.
accepted.tq: Use the sequence of registration and merger to reject swapped dates and organisations.
accepted.sec: BharatNet - phases, implementing agency, GP target, amended programme

accepted.s: BharatNet has been laid by which group of Central Public Sector Undertakings?
accepted.x: The BharatNet network has been laid by the CPSUs BSNL, RailTel and Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (PGCIL).
accepted.tq: Identify the correct implementing-agency combination rather than a related ministry or institution.
accepted.sec: BharatNet - phases, implementing agency, GP target, amended programme

accepted.s: The target bandwidth under BharatNet is:
o: 10 Mbps per gram panchayat, scalable to 100 Mbps
100 Mbps per village, fixed without scalability
100 Mbps per gram panchayat, scalable to 1 Gbps
1 Gbps per gram panchayat, scalable to 10 Gbps
accepted.x: BharatNet targets 100 Mbps for each gram panchayat, with scalability up to 1 Gbps.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the base capacity from the scalable capacity in a two-number technical target.
accepted.sec: BharatNet - phases, implementing agency, GP target, amended programme

accepted.s: As of March 2025, which of the following correctly represents the reported BharatNet status?
o: 2,50,000 gram panchayats connected and 5.92 lakh km of optical fibre cable laid
2,18,347 villages connected and 9.62 lakh km of optical fibre cable laid
2,18,347 gram panchayats connected and 6.92 lakh km of optical fibre cable laid
1,18,347 gram panchayats connected and 6.92 lakh km of optical fibre cable laid
accepted.x: The reported March 2025 status was 2,18,347 connected gram panchayats and 6.92 lakh kilometres of optical fibre cable.
accepted.tq: Match two quantitative status indicators without confusing gram panchayats with villages.
accepted.sec: BharatNet - phases, implementing agency, GP target, amended programme

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Phases I and II of BharatNet?
o: They focused on fibre connectivity to gram panchayats through CPSUs and States.
They focused exclusively on upgrading 480 new gram panchayats.
They were limited to last-mile Wi-Fi through private cloud providers.
They primarily introduced a PPP model with revenue sharing and 5G links.
accepted.x: Phases I and II, beginning from 2011, focused on providing fibre connectivity to gram panchayats through CPSUs and States.
accepted.tq: Separate the focus of the earlier phases from the features of the amended programme.
accepted.sec: BharatNet - phases, implementing agency, GP target, amended programme

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature associated with Phase III or the Amended BharatNet Programme?
o: Exclusive implementation through CPSUs without private participation
Revenue sharing and last-mile links with 5G
accepted.x: The Amended BharatNet Programme provides for a PPP model, a greater role for States, revenue sharing, last-mile connectivity and links with 5G. It is not exclusively implemented through CPSUs without private participation.
accepted.tq: Find the option that contradicts the distinguishing features of the amended phase.
accepted.sec: BharatNet - phases, implementing agency, GP target, amended programme

accepted.s: The approved outlay associated with Phase III or the Amended BharatNet Programme is:
accepted.x: The Amended BharatNet Programme is associated with an outlay of Rs 1.39 lakh crore.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the programme-wide outlay from the separate Andhra Pradesh commitment.
accepted.sec: BharatNet - phases, implementing agency, GP target, amended programme

accepted.s: On 22 February 2026, the Memorandum of Cooperation concerning BharatNet in Andhra Pradesh was signed at:
accepted.x: The Memorandum of Cooperation was signed in Amaravati between the Digital Bharat Nidhi Administrator and the Government of Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Recall the specific location attached to a state-level digital infrastructure agreement.
accepted.sec: BharatNet - phases, implementing agency, GP target, amended programme

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the scope of the Andhra Pradesh BharatNet agreement of February 2026?
o: 1,692 Phase-I GPs upgraded, 11,254 Phase-II villages covered and 480 new GPs added
1,692 new GPs added, 11,254 Phase-I GPs upgraded and 480 villages covered
13,426 Phase-I GPs upgraded and no new GPs added
480 Phase-I GPs upgraded, 1,692 Phase-II villages covered and 11,254 new GPs added
accepted.x: The stated scope includes upgrading 1,692 Phase-I gram panchayats, covering 11,254 Phase-II villages and adding 480 new gram panchayats.
accepted.tq: Keep the three numerical components aligned with their respective categories.
accepted.sec: BharatNet - phases, implementing agency, GP target, amended programme

accepted.s: The state special purpose vehicle identified for implementing the Andhra Pradesh BharatNet agreement is:
accepted.x: The state SPV is Andhra Pradesh BharatNet Infrastructure Ltd.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact institutional name instead of a plausible but unlisted corporation.
accepted.sec: BharatNet - phases, implementing agency, GP target, amended programme

accepted.s: PMGDISHA was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at:
accepted.x: PMGDISHA was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at Gandhinagar.
accepted.tq: Recall the launch venue of a named government digital-literacy scheme.
accepted.sec: PMGDISHA - target group, coverage, age, certification

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the target and age group under PMGDISHA?
o: Two crore rural households, one person per household, aged 14–50 years
Six crore rural households, all persons per household, aged 18–59 years
Six crore urban households, two persons per household, aged 18–60 years
Six crore rural households, one person per household, aged 14–60 years
accepted.x: PMGDISHA targeted six crore rural households, with one person from each household, in the age group of 14 to 60 years.
accepted.tq: Check target population, household coverage and age range as separate components.
accepted.sec: PMGDISHA - target group, coverage, age, certification

accepted.s: PMGDISHA closed on 31 March 2024. Which set of figures correctly represents its registered, trained and certified beneficiaries, respectively?
accepted.x: At closure, PMGDISHA had 7.35 crore registered beneficiaries, 6.39 crore trained beneficiaries and 4.78 crore certified beneficiaries.
accepted.tq: Preserve the order of registration, training and certification while comparing close figures.
accepted.sec: PMGDISHA - target group, coverage, age, certification

accepted.s: MeghRaj refers to which of the following?
o: A public Wi-Fi programme initiated by DoT
A rural optical-fibre programme initiated by BSNL
The GI Cloud initiated by DeitY
A digital-literacy mission initiated by NCERT
accepted.x: MeghRaj is the GI Cloud initiative started by the Department of Electronics and Information Technology (DeitY).
accepted.tq: Expand and identify the exact identity and originating authority of an ICT initiative.
accepted.sec: MeghRaj GI Cloud - architecture, empanelment

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes the GI Cloud under MeghRaj?
o: A certification platform for digital-literacy trainees
A common pool of cloud infrastructure and applications available on demand
A fixed database accessible only to private companies
A satellite network for village connectivity
accepted.x: MeghRaj provides a common pool of cloud infrastructure and applications that departments can access on demand. It is intended to provide secure and scalable ICT for government departments.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the functional nature of a cloud platform from connectivity and certification schemes.
accepted.sec: MeghRaj GI Cloud - architecture, empanelment

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the five characteristics of cloud computing identified under MeghRaj?
o: Mandatory physical installation for every user
accepted.x: The five characteristics are on-demand self-service, ubiquitous network access, metered use, elasticity and resource pooling. Mandatory physical installation for every user is not one of them.
accepted.tq: Find the non-cloud characteristic among the standard feature list.
accepted.sec: MeghRaj GI Cloud - architecture, empanelment

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. IaaS — Infrastructure as a Service
2. PaaS — Platform as a Service
3. SaaS — Software as a Service
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All three pairs are correctly matched and constitute the three service models listed for MeghRaj: IaaS, PaaS and SaaS.
accepted.tq: Expand technical abbreviations and verify each pair before selecting the combined option.
accepted.sec: MeghRaj GI Cloud - architecture, empanelment

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a deployment model of MeghRaj GI Cloud?
accepted.x: The four deployment models are public, private, hybrid and community cloud. Satellite cloud is not one of the listed deployment models.
accepted.tq: Use the exact four-item classification and reject the invented category.
accepted.sec: MeghRaj GI Cloud - architecture, empanelment

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the architecture and empanelment arrangements under MeghRaj?
o: Only private clouds are permitted and no application store is included.
MeitY empanels private Cloud Service Providers; the architecture includes national and State clouds and an e-Gov App Store.
State governments empanel foreign providers without involvement of MeitY.
The architecture consists only of a single national cloud operated by BSNL.
accepted.x: MeitY empanels private Cloud Service Providers for government use. The architecture includes national and State clouds along with an e-Gov App Store.
accepted.tq: Check the responsible authority and the complete architecture rather than accepting a partial description.
accepted.sec: MeghRaj GI Cloud - architecture, empanelment

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the Samriddh Gram pilot location?
accepted.x: The Samriddh Gram pilots include Narakoduru in Andhra Pradesh, Ari and Umri in Madhya Pradesh, and Chaurawala in Uttar Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Use location-state matching to distinguish the four pilot sites.
accepted.sec: Digital Village pilot - CSC-led services

accepted.s: The Samriddh Gram pilots were associated with which of the following?
o: Only State government data centres and agreements concluded in February 2023
Telecom Centres of Excellence and agreements concluded in October 2025
MeghRaj cloud providers and agreements concluded in March 2024
The PMGDISHA certification network and agreements concluded in December 2020
accepted.x: The Samriddh Gram pilots were associated with Telecom Centres of Excellence, with agreements concluded in October 2025.
accepted.tq: Link a pilot programme to its institutional framework and time reference.
accepted.sec: Digital Village pilot - CSC-led services

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT listed among the services offered by the AP Samriddhi Kendra at Narakoduru?
accepted.x: The AP Samriddhi Kendra offers passport and Aadhaar services, bill payments, soil testing, drone spraying and AI training. Issuance of international driving licences is not listed.
accepted.tq: Find the service that falls outside the stated CSC-led service basket.
accepted.sec: Digital Village pilot - CSC-led services

accepted.s: Gujarat's Digital Seva Setu provides services through e-Gram centres to:
accepted.x: Gujarat's Digital Seva Setu brings 321 services to more than 14,078 gram panchayats through e-Gram centres.
accepted.tq: Keep the service count distinct from the number of gram panchayats covered.
accepted.sec: Digital Village pilot - CSC-led services

accepted.s: The Universal Service Obligation Fund (USOF) was primarily intended to support telecommunications in:
o: commercially unviable rural and remote areas
government offices located only in State capitals
foreign markets with high private investment
accepted.x: USOF is a non-lapsable fund intended to support telecommunications in commercially unviable rural and remote areas.
accepted.tq: Apply the purpose of a public connectivity fund to an area-selection scenario.
accepted.sec: Rural connectivity funds - USOF / Digital Bharat Nidhi, LWE towers, PM-WANI

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about USOF and Digital Bharat Nidhi is correct?
o: USOF was renamed Digital Bharat Nidhi under the Telecommunications Act, 2023, and it funded NOFN.
Digital Bharat Nidhi was renamed USOF under the Telecommunications Act, 2023, and it funded PMGDISHA.
USOF is a lapsable fund used only for urban 5G deployment.
Digital Bharat Nidhi is administered only by State governments and has no relation to BharatNet.
accepted.x: USOF funded NOFN and was renamed Digital Bharat Nidhi under the Telecommunications Act, 2023. Digital Bharat Nidhi also runs the Amended BharatNet Memoranda of Cooperation.
accepted.tq: Track the renaming direction and distinguish the fund's actual connectivity uses.
accepted.sec: Rural connectivity funds - USOF / Digital Bharat Nidhi, LWE towers, PM-WANI

accepted.s: Approximately what share of Digital Bharat Nidhi collections is allocated to the Telecom Technology Development Fund?
o: 5 percent, approximately Rs 500 crore per year
10 percent, approximately Rs 1,000 crore per year
1 percent, approximately Rs 100 crore per year
25 percent, approximately Rs 2,500 crore per year
accepted.x: Five percent of Digital Bharat Nidhi collections, approximately Rs 500 crore per year, goes to the Telecom Technology Development Fund.
accepted.tq: Match the percentage with its approximate annual monetary value.
accepted.sec: Rural connectivity funds - USOF / Digital Bharat Nidhi, LWE towers, PM-WANI

accepted.s: The Memoranda of Cooperation for the Amended BharatNet Programme are run through which fund?
accepted.x: Digital Bharat Nidhi runs the Memoranda of Cooperation for the Amended BharatNet Programme.
accepted.tq: Identify the funding channel linked to a specific infrastructure programme.
accepted.sec: Rural connectivity funds - USOF / Digital Bharat Nidhi, LWE towers, PM-WANI

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes PM-WANI?
o: A digital-literacy programme launched in December 2020, covering 6 crore households.
A fibre-laying programme launched in October 2011, covering 2.5 lakh gram panchayats.
A cloud deployment model launched in March 2024, with 3.15 crore applications.
A public Wi-Fi programme launched in December 2020, with 3.15 lakh hotspots reported.
accepted.x: PM-WANI is a public Wi-Fi initiative launched in December 2020, with 3.15 lakh hotspots reported.
accepted.tq: Separate the programme's technology, launch date and scale from other digital initiatives.
accepted.sec: Rural connectivity funds - USOF / Digital Bharat Nidhi, LWE towers, PM-WANI
